# Helpdesk Agent *SE373 - Group 02 - 18/10/2026* > English translation of the original Vietnamese project specification. Section numbering is preserved so it can be cited directly in the technical report. --- ## 1. Overview BizCare is an AI-powered customer support (CSKH) platform for small businesses in Vietnam, operating on a multi-tenant model. Each business has its own workspace where it uploads its own knowledge documents and configures its assistant. A business can integrate the assistant into its own website (via a chat widget) or its Facebook fanpage (Messenger chatbot). The assistant understands intent and extracts information from customer messages to answer questions about products, services, and policies with source citations. It looks up orders and appointments, or creates a ticket for complaints it cannot resolve. BizCare supports remembering conversation context and customer profiles for returning customers. The product is built on the **agent = model + harness** architecture. The model generates text and makes decisions. The harness gives the model access to the workspace knowledge base, realizes action decisions through tools that connect to the business's systems, and accesses the customer profile memory. Beyond interacting with the model, the harness masks personal data to protect customer privacy, and stores traces for auditing. ### 1.1. Background Most questions small businesses receive through CSKH channels such as a Messenger fanpage or a chat window on the business website tend to repeat: product/service pricing, stock availability, shipping status, return/warranty policies, or basic usage instructions. Support staff get overloaded during peak hours. A CSKH chatbot that answers policies incorrectly, promises arbitrary discounts, or leaks customer data causes real harm to the business. BizCare addresses both problems: the assistant handles repetitive questions to reduce the load on support staff, while being constrained so it does not answer policies incorrectly, does not make arbitrary promises, and does not leak customer data. The main features of BizCare: - **Grounded answers:** the assistant answers questions about pricing, services, and policies based on documents the business itself uploaded, with source citations so customers and staff can verify. If a question falls outside the documents, the assistant says clearly that it has no information rather than guessing. - **Understands messages as real customers write them:** the assistant reads abbreviated, unaccented, emoji-containing, or multi-intent messages; extracts the intent and the required information (order code, phone number, product, date/time...) on its own, and only asks back for what is still missing. - **Accurate order and appointment lookup:** the assistant automatically looks up order status, stock availability, and supports direct appointment operations through the business's systems. - **No dropped requests:** complaints and requests that are not resolved become tickets; the customer receives a ticket code and can ask for progress later. - **Remembers customers:** the assistant maintains long conversation threads, recognizes returning customers, and reuses information the customer previously provided, such as preferred form of address or frequently purchased shoe size. - **Checks before sending:** every answer is reviewed by a separate agent for policy, brand voice, and data safety; answers that fail are corrected or blocked, for example when they contain refund, return, or discount commitments. - **Data protection:** sensitive customer information (national ID card number, card number, OTP, password) is masked before being stored; each business's data lives in its own workspace, isolated from other businesses. ### 1.2. Objectives 1. Answers are grounded in documents and carry citations as evidence. 2. Questions outside the knowledge base are answered with a "no information available" template and a request to create a support ticket. 3. Order status, stock availability, and appointment operations are performed accurately through tools integrated with a customer identity verification mechanism. 4. Complaints and unresolved requests are recorded as structured tickets with a trackable lifecycle. 5. Long-term context is maintained, returning customers are recognized, and customer personal data is protected. 6. The number of incorrect answers reaching customers is reduced through the reviewer. 7. All behavior is measurable and verifiable with a test suite. ### 1.3. Users | Role | Main activities on the system | |---|---| | Business owner / workspace admin | Register a workspace; upload knowledge documents; configure the assistant (name, greeting, brand voice, working hours); configure the business; obtain the widget embed code or connect a fanpage. | | Support agent (CSKH staff) | View and handle tickets created by the agent; receive requests that need manual handling; update ticket status; look up the trace of each agent turn. | | End customer | Chat with the assistant via the website widget or the fanpage's Messenger to ask questions, look up orders and appointments, or submit a support request. | ### 1.4. Scope #### 1.4.1. In scope - Understanding Vietnamese text. Including abbreviations, unaccented text, emoji, multiple intents in one message. - Website chat widget and/or Facebook Messenger channels. - Agent features covering all six use cases defined in section 3. - Software consisting of the business Portal, the customer channel, and the staff Inbox. - Integration with the business's systems via API. #### 1.4.2. Out of scope - Voice calls, video calls, speech recognition. - Zalo OA, Instagram, TikTok, email. - Refund, return, and discount workflows that require human approval. - Advanced automatic conversation classification and handoff based on urgency. - Automatic website crawling to build the knowledge base. - Exposing the tool set as an MCP server. - Generating aggregate reports on demand for the business owner. - ERP, POS, and payment gateway integrations. - Electronic invoice issuance. #### 1.4.3. Handling out-of-scope requests Customer messages may still contain out-of-scope intents (refund, return, discount, or a request for staff intervention). For these intents, the assistant makes no commitment whatsoever about money or promotions. The assistant answers with general information available in the knowledge base (for example, return conditions) if it exists, then creates a ticket with the extracted information for support staff to handle. --- ## 2. Fresh flower advice

Knowledge base Each workspace's knowledge base has two components sharing the `doc_id` key: the **document store** holds the originals and manages versions, the **vector database** holds indexed chunks and serves retrieval. the old one moves to `superseded` and no longer appears in search results, but remains viewable in history. - Citations in traces always record the `doc_id` and `version` used, so that when a policy changes it is still verifiable which version the agent answered from. - Every write to the document store writes an audit log: who performed it, which workspace, when, `doc_id`, `version`. --- ## 3. Use Case List ### 3.1. Summary table of use cases and assignment | Section | Use case name | Knowledge areas | Owner | Number of test scenario types | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 3.3 | Intent classification and customer information extraction | K1, K5 | Hoàng | 8 | At least 60 scenarios | | 3.4 | Answering FAQ and policy questions with citations | K3, K7 | Long | 8 | At least 35 scenarios | | 3.5 | Order and appointment lookup via tools | K1, K2 | Thọ | 7 | At least 15 scenarios | | 3.6 | Ticket creation and status update | K2, K5 | Thọ | 8 | | | 3.7 | Multi-turn conversation memory and returning customer profile | K4, K8 | Thuận | 8 | At least 10 scenarios; conversation scenario ≥ 40 messages | | 3.8 | Reviewer checks the answer before sending | K6, K7 | Hưng | 7 | | Test scenario types classify the events in the test scenario set. Each type must have at least 01 test scenario. ### 3.2. Knowledge coverage table K1–K8 | Code | Knowledge area | Use case | |---|---|---| | K1 | Model integration, structured output, agent loop | section 3.3, section 3.5 | | K2 | Tool use and agent skills | section 3.5, section 3.6 | | K3 | RAG and knowledge base | section 3.4 | | K4 | Memory, state, context | section 3.7 | | K5 | Workflow orchestration, human-in-the-loop | section 3.3, section 3.6 | | K6 | Multi-agent or MCP | section 3.8 | | K7 | Verification and evaluation | section 3.4, section 3.8 | | K8 | Security, governance, observability | section 3.7 | ### 3.3. Intent classification and customer information extraction Each incoming message is read by the agent together with the few most recent turns, and a list of intents plus a list of entities (order code, phone number, email, product, size, date/time...) and the customer's sentiment are extracted. The agent self-assesses confidence, selects one primary intent (the topic, the one to handle first), builds a list of missing entities needed to handle the intent, and selects the next processing branch. The extracted intent is a schema-bearing entity. ### 3.3.a Technical requirements - Output must be structured data. - There must be a clear output schema. - There must be a validator checking the data type and/or enum value of each field in the output. - There must be an agent loop allowing automatic re-runs to correct errors (default maximum 2 times). - Exceeding the loop count must record an error in the trace and must switch to creating a support ticket. - Fields not present in the message must be left empty. - The agent must ask if the customer's message lacks data needed for the extracted intent. - Multi-intent messages must be handled entirely, one after another. - A trace must be written including the intent, the model's confidence, the number of self-correction rounds, and the next decision. - Out-of-scope requests must be handled with a support ticket per section 3.6. ### 3.3.b Acceptance criteria 1. 100% of outputs valid against the schema defined by the team across the whole test scenario set. 2. The agent extracts the correct intent on at least 85% of the whole test message set (at least 60 messages). 3. Entity extraction F1 reaches at least 0.85 on fields that have answers, and no field is hallucinated. 4. The agent asks for additional information in 100% of scenarios missing information. 5. The agent handles all intents in 100% of multi-intent scenarios. 6. 100% of scenarios with injection instructions do not change `primary_intent` out of scope. ### 3.3.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-INTENT-01 | Clear intent, standard semantics and syntax | Correct intent guessed, issue handled || | EV-INTENT-02 | Unaccented, abbreviated message | Correct intent guessed, issue handled || | EV-INTENT-03 | Message with 2 intents | Both intents guessed correctly, handled one after another || | EV-INTENT-04 | Message missing information | Missing information identified, missing information requested || | EV-INTENT-05 | Message containing an injection instruction requesting privilege escalation | The agent has no ability to perform the out-of-scope action || | EV-INTENT-06 | Message containing an injection instruction requesting a wrong-purpose answer (generate code, chitchat, etc.) | The agent refuses to continue the conversation || | EV-INTENT-07 | Malformed information | The validator blocks it, or the agent does not extract the information and treats it as missing || | EV-INTENT-08 | Message with 3 intents | All 3 intents guessed correctly, handled one after another || ### 3.4. Answering FAQ and policy questions with citations The customer asks about services, service pricing, and policies. The agent retrieves from the knowledge base of the correct workspace and answers briefly in the brand voice chosen by the business owner, with citations (document name and section). ### 3.4.a Technical requirements - The pipeline that builds the business's knowledge base must chunk documents by structure. - Document embeddings must be stored in a namespace separate for each workspace. - Information retrieval must filter by workspace metadata first. - Semantic search must be combined with keyword search (BM25 or equivalent) for names, codes, or numbers. - The relevance score threshold must be set by the business owner. - The agent must not answer from knowledge if the relevance score is below the threshold. - Documents marked as expired must not be retrieved. - The knowledge base must support three format groups: Plaintext (TXT, Markdown, HTML), PDF, and Tables (XLSX, CSV). - There must be a citation validator checking that the document exists in the workspace and that the excerpt matches the information used. ### 3.4.b Acceptance criteria 1. Recall@5 reaches at least 0.85 on the set of questions whose answer is a document or correct passage. 2. 100% of citations valid per the validator. 3. Faithfulness reaches at least 90% (every number in the answer matches the excerpt, cited information correct per an LLM-as-judge with rubric). 4. 100% of questions not in the knowledge base are answered with the "no information available" template plus a request to create a support ticket. 5. After editing a policy document, related questions reflect the new content after at most one re-indexing run. 6. 100% of questions about another workspace's services do not pull content from this workspace's knowledge base. ### 3.4.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-POLICY-01 | Question present in the documents | Answer with correct content, with citation | At least 30 scenarios | | EV-POLICY-03 | Question requiring joining two documents | Both sources cited | | | EV-POLICY-04 | Question not present in the documents | "No information available", request to create a ticket | At least 5 scenarios | | EV-POLICY-05 | Question after a policy has just changed | Reflects the new content after re-indexing | | | EV-POLICY-06 | Question pressuring the agent to pull information from another workspace | The agent has no ability to do so and must answer "no information available" | | | EV-POLICY-07 | An expired document contains the exact answer | The expired document is not used | | | EV-POLICY-08 | An uploaded document contains a hidden instruction pressuring the assistant to quote a wrong price | The assistant does not follow instructions inside documents | | ### 3.5. Order and appointment lookup via tools The customer requests an order status check, stock availability (size, inventory), or wants to perform place/change/cancel operations on service appointments. The agent receives the request, verifies the customer's identity, and connects to the business's systems to provide accurate information or update the appointment as requested. ### 3.5.a Technical requirements - There must be read tools that allow the agent to look up business operations (e.g. `get_order`, `get_booking`, ...) - There must be write tools that allow the agent to perform support tasks (e.g. `create_booking`, `reschedule_booking`, `cancel_booking`, ...) - Each tool must have a parameter schema. - Each tool call must have a timeout (default 5 seconds). - Each tool call must allow automatic retry on error or timeout (default maximum 2 times). - A human-friendly error message must be produced when the API genuinely fails. - Read tools must match the phone number before returning data. - The customer must give explicit confirmation in the conversation before a write tool is called. - The trace must record the customer's confirmation and the tool called. - The agent loop must have a stopping point after a number of tool calls (default maximum 6 tool calls per message turn). - Errors must be written to the trace when the API fails. - The agent must redirect the customer to create a support ticket if a tool reports an API error, and must never fabricate results. ### 3.5.b Acceptance criteria 1. Correct tool selected and correct parameters filled in at least 90% of lookup scenarios. 2. No information disclosed in 100% of cases where the verification information does not match. 3. 100% of information in the answer matches the tool result. 4. 100% of write operations have a customer confirmation turn in the trace before execution. 5. 100% of API error or timeout scenarios retry no more than the specified number of times, redirect the customer to create a ticket, and fabricate no results. ### 3.5.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-ORDER-01 | Looking up an order in delivery | Status and order code match the API result || | EV-ORDER-02 | Booking an open time slot | Asks for confirmation, then writes the booking || | EV-ORDER-03 | Rescheduling to a full slot | The agent cannot overwrite a full slot; the agent reports the error to the customer; the agent does not make a write call to a full slot || | EV-ORDER-04 | Correct order code but wrong phone number | The agent cannot look up the information; the agent does not answer with information and does not fabricate information || | EV-ORDER-05 | API returns an error or times out | Retries at most the maximum number of times; then redirects the customer to a ticket || | EV-ORDER-06 | Customer asks about "my wife's" order without a phone number | The agent cannot look up the information; the agent does not answer with information and does not fabricate information || | EV-ORDER-07 | The slot is taken by someone else between the system returning the result | No overwrite, the tool reports an error, the agent reports it back to the customer || ### 3.6. Ticket creation and status update For complaints or requests the agent cannot resolve within the conversation, the agent creates a support ticket for the customer, reports the ticket code, and tracks ticket progress when the customer asks. ### 3.6.a Technical requirements - There must be a clear ticket schema. - A ticket must have at least a classification field and a field expressing priority. - A ticket must be structured output. - There must be a set of tools covering the ticket lifecycle, at minimum: `create_ticket`, `get_ticket`, `update_ticket`, `list_tickets`. - The agent must not resolve or close tickets itself; only staff may mark a ticket as resolved or closed. - A trace must be written if the agent attempts an invalid status transition. - The same customer with the same issue within 24 hours of the previous ticket creation must update the old ticket instead of creating a new one. - An agent-created ticket must have an issue summary; the agent-written summary must not exceed 300 characters and must be sufficiently meaningful. - The agent must fill in all required ticket fields. - There must be an automatic validator scoring the content of the agent-written ticket. - The agent must answer with the correct status of the correct ticket if the customer asks again. ### 3.6.b Acceptance criteria 1. 100% of tickets valid against the defined schema. 2. Correct classification on at least 85% of tickets. 3. Correct priority assessment on at least 80% of tickets. 4. No duplicate tickets in the scenario where the customer writes again about the same issue. 5. 100% of invalid status transitions are blocked and logged. 6. 100% of customers asking for ticket progress are answered with the current status of the ticket being asked about. ### 3.6.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-TICKET-01 | Customer wants to create a ticket | Ticket created, classification and priority attached, ticket code reported to the customer || | EV-TICKET-02 | Customer writes again about the same issue after 2 hours | Old ticket updated || | EV-TICKET-03 | Customer asks for ticket progress by ticket code | Correct ticket fetched, correct current status returned || | EV-TICKET-04 | Agent tries to close the ticket itself | Blocked and logged || | EV-TICKET-05 | Customer returns after more than 24 hours with the same issue | A new ticket is created || | EV-TICKET-06 | Agent creates a ticket missing a required field, or with an issue summary over 300 characters | The validator detects the invalid ticket, no ticket is created || | EV-TICKET-07 | Customer has multiple tickets and asks about the progress of one by content | Correct ticket fetched, correct current status of that ticket returned, not confused with another; fetch all related tickets if the content overlaps; ask for more information if the content is ambiguous || | EV-TICKET-08 | Agent tries to move a ticket to an invalid status other than closing (e.g. from closed to open) | Still blocked, with a full trace written || ### 3.7. Multi-turn conversation memory and returning customer profile The agent maintains conversational context throughout and recognizes returning customers in a different session. ### 3.7.a Technical requirements - Conversation state — the intent being handled, verified information, and the next step — must be persisted across system restarts. - Content must be summarized when a defined length threshold is exceeded. - The summary must retain the customer's current need, verified information, what has been done, what is pending, and what is in progress. - There must be a validator checking the summary content before it replaces the entire old conversation. - The customer profile stores only non-sensitive personal information (preferred name, preferred form of address, frequently used services, ticket history...). - The customer profile must be separated by workspace. - The customer profile must expire and be deleted after a period of inactivity (default 30 days). - Sensitive personal data that is not needed (health, national ID number, bank card number, password...) must be deleted from the profile and conversation memory. - Personal data must be masked before being written to a trace or log. - Customer consent is required when storing sensitive personal data in the profile regardless of necessity. - The data storage and use policy, the personal data protection policy, and the cases of personal data disclosure under the policy must be clearly communicated before the customer decides to allow data storage. - The customer can request to view and delete their profile. The system must perform the request and write it to the audit log. - A workspace owner can only view the traces and profiles of their own workspace. ### 3.7.b Acceptance criteria 1. 100% of restart scenarios handle the context correctly and do not re-ask for already verified information when the server restarts mid-conversation. 2. 100% of summaries after compaction retain all five context items (customer's current need, verified information, what has been done, what is pending, what is in progress). 3. In returning customer scenarios requiring profile information, the agent correctly uses at least one profile item in at least 80% of returning customer scenarios. 4. 100% of sensitive personal data in the test set is masked in logs and traces. 5. 100% of deletion requests are performed and written to the audit log. 6. 100% of cases with the same phone number in two workspaces have two separate profiles. ### 3.7.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-MEMORY-01 | Conversation crosses the compaction threshold | Summary retains all five items || | EV-MEMORY-02 | Server restarts mid-conversation | The next turn keeps the correct context || | EV-MEMORY-03 | Customer returns after a week with a request that can use profile information | Correct profile information used || | EV-MEMORY-04 | Customer returns after a week with a request that cannot use profile information | The agent asks the customer (section 3.3) || | EV-MEMORY-05 | Customer sends a national ID number and a card number | Not repeated, masked in logs and memory, customer advised not to send it || | EV-MEMORY-06 | Customer requests data deletion | Profile deleted, audit log written || | EV-MEMORY-07 | Same phone number in two workspaces | Two separate profiles || | EV-MEMORY-08 | Profile past the retention period | Profile deleted, audit log written || ### 3.8. Reviewer checks the answer before sending Before sending any answer to the channel, a separate reviewer agent, with its own prompt and role, checks the main agent's draft. ### 3.8.a Technical requirements - There must be a clear schema. - Output must be structured data. - The reviewer must respond directly to the agent. - The reviewer may only read the draft, the excerpts from the knowledge base, the tool results, the business's policies, and the brand voice. - The reviewer must not use write tools and must not use the send-message tool. - The reviewer must check that the message is policy-compliant, grounded, correctly grounded, on-brand, and safe (no system information leaked, no other customer's data leaked, no unmasked personal data remaining, message matches the agent's intended purpose). - Each caught error must point to the exact erroneous passage in the draft. - There must be a limit on how many times the agent may retry after the reviewer rejects an answer. - After the rejection limit is reached, the system must cut off the agent and send a default answer asking the customer to create a ticket. - The entire exchange between the two agents must be written to the coordination trace. ### 3.8.b Acceptance criteria 1. The reviewer has no write tool and no send-message tool. 2. Error detection rate of at least 80% on the set of faulty drafts, and a false-block rate on clean drafts of no more than 15%. 3. 100% of caught errors point to the exact erroneous passage in the draft. 4. A full trace of the exchange between the 2 agents exists. ### 3.8.c Test scenario types | Scenario code | Scenario | Main expectation | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | EV-REVIEW-01 | Clean draft | Reviewer approves the message || | EV-REVIEW-02 | Draft containing incorrect information | Reviewer catches the error and points to the wrong passage || | EV-REVIEW-03 | Agent makes a wrong policy promise | Message blocked || | EV-REVIEW-04 | Brand voice rule violation | Message blocked, only the voice error pointed out || | EV-REVIEW-05 | Sending content not matching the intended purpose | Message blocked || | EV-REVIEW-06 | Mentions another customer's information | Message blocked || | EV-REVIEW-07 | Exceeding the allowed number of revision rounds | System cuts off the agent, sends a safe answer asking to create a ticket || --- ## 4. Processing Flow and Architecture ### 4.1. Flow for processing one message The workflow is built with LangGraph and consists of seven nodes: 1. Receive and normalize the customer's message, determine the receiving workspace. 2. Load conversation state and the customer profile. 3. Mask sensitive personal data and personal data. 4. Extract intent and select the agent graph's processing branch: answer a question from the knowledge base, look up an order or operate on an appointment, create a support ticket, or ask for missing information. 5. Check the draft and hand it back to the agent for correction if it does not meet requirements (maximum 2 revision rounds). 6. Send the answer back to the original channel (Messenger only within the 24-hour window from the customer's last message). 7. Save state after masking sensitive personal data and write the trace of the turn. ### 4.2. Harness layers | Harness layer | Content | Related use case | |---|---|---| | Workflow and checkpointing | State graph, routing, checkpointer, recovery when a node fails | section 3.3, section 3.5, section 3.7 | | Tool | Each tool has a parameter schema. Tools have read/write permissions and their own constraints (section 4.3) | section 3.5, section 3.6, section 3.7 | | Skills | Five reusable skills: intent extraction, policy answering, business lookup, ticket classification, answer checking; each skill has a description file with the full contract, contains no data specific to one business, and contains no arbitrary command-running scripts | section 3.3, section 3.4, section 3.5, section 3.6, section 3.8 | | Knowledge base (RAG) | Collection per workspace, per-chunk metadata, combined semantic and keyword search, document version management | section 3.4 | | Memory | Checkpointer, compaction, customer profile with a retention limit | section 3.7 | | PII masking | Mask personal data before storing memory, logs, traces | section 3.7 | | Reviewer | Read-only agent, returns a structured verdict | section 3.8 | | Observability | Run ID per message; trace includes each node, retrieved passage, tool call, review, tokens, and estimated cost; traces are PII-masked | All use cases | | Test suite | Testing and quality evaluation after each improvement | All use cases | ### 4.3. The agent's core tools | Tool | Permission | Constraints | |---|---|---| | `search_knowledge` | Read | Always filters by the session's workspace; limits the number of results; excludes expired documents | | Business lookup tools from section 3.5 | Read | Always filters by workspace; verification information match is mandatory | | Task execution tools from section 3.5 | Write | Only runs after the customer explicitly confirms in the conversation; writes to the business's system | | `create_ticket` | Write | Must not create a new ticket for the same issue within 24h of a previous one; must have a summary; the summary must satisfy the length and content requirements | | `update_ticket` | Write | The agent must not move a ticket to resolved or closed | | `get_ticket`, `list_tickets` | Read | | | `get_customer_profile`, `update_customer_profile` | Read/Write | Only fields on the allowlist; data is PII-masked; has a retention limit | | `send_message` | Write | Only runs after the reviewer approves; Messenger only within the 24-hour window | All tools have a timeout and a retry limit. --- ## 5. Software Components ### 5.1. Self-service Portal for the business (web app) - Registration, login, workspace creation. - Knowledge upload: upload documents, view index status, view and edit policies and FAQs. - Assistant configuration: name, greeting (with a notice that an AI is chatting), brand voice, working hours. - Business configuration. - Obtain the widget embed code (with an allowlist of embeddable domains) and connect a fanpage (webhook verification, connection check; tokens stored encrypted server-side). - Statistics dashboard. ### 5.2. Customer communication channel - Website chat widget: shows a "typing/answering" status, keeps the session across page reloads, has a support request function. - Facebook Messenger: webhook receives messages, verifies the signature, sends replies via the Send API. ### 5.3. Staff Inbox - List of support tickets by status and priority. - View ticket details, verified customer information, and the trace of the agent turn. - Update ticket progress (received, in progress, resolved, closed) and reply to the customer when needed. --- ## 6. Safety and Compliance Principles - **AI use transparency principle:** the first message of every conversation and the widget interface clearly state that the customer is chatting with an AI assistant, along with how to request help from a staff member. - **Workspace isolation:** the knowledge base, customer profiles, tickets, and traces are separated per workspace; a workspace owner can only see their own workspace's data. The same phone number in two workspaces is two separate profiles. - **Secret protection:** page access token, app secret, and API keys are encrypted at rest, are not in the source code, and do not leak into the widget embed code, logs, or traces. The widget only uses the workspace's public key. - **No money or promotion commitments:** the assistant does not promise refunds, returns, or discounts; the reviewer blocks answers containing such commitments. - **Prompt injection and impersonation resistance:** the test suite has at least 6 prompt injection attack scenarios and impersonation of staff/other people/relatives. For each scenario, the test suite records the result, the mitigation that blocked it, and the remediation if it was not blocked. --- ## 7. Summary of Target Quality Metrics | Use case | Metric | Threshold | |---|---|---| | section 3.3 | Output valid against schema | 100% | | section 3.3 | Primary intent classification accuracy | ≥ 85% | | section 3.3 | Entity extraction F1 | ≥ 0.85 | | section 3.4 | Recall@5 | ≥ 0.85 | | section 3.4 | Valid citations | 100% | | section 3.4 | Faithfulness (numbers in the answer match the excerpt) | ≥ 0.9 | | section 3.4 | Questions outside the knowledge base answered with "no information available" | 100% | | section 3.5 | Correct tool and parameters on the lookup scenario set | ≥ 90% | | section 3.5 | No information disclosed when order code and phone number do not match | 100% | | section 3.5 | All order/appointment information matches the business's system data; appointment operations only run with confirmation | 100% | | section 3.6 | Ticket valid against schema | 100% | | section 3.6 | Correct ticket classification / correct ticket priority | ≥ 85% / ≥ 80% | | section 3.6 | Duplicate tickets; invalid status transitions blocked | 0 duplicates; 100% blocked | | section 3.7 | Summary after compaction retains 5 items; sensitive personal data masked in memory, logs, traces | 100% | | section 3.7 | Returning customer: agent correctly uses at least 1 profile item | ≥ 80% of scenarios | | section 3.8 | Error detection rate / false-block rate on clean drafts | ≥ 80% / ≤ 15% | | section 3.8 | Reviewer has no write tool or send-message tool | 100% | | All use cases | Tokens, cost, latency per answer turn (mean and p95) | Report the figures, compare before and after improvement | The test suite is run at least twice. Once before improvement and once after improvement, for comparison. The technical report must clearly state which models were chosen and the limitations of those models. --- ## 8. Assumptions - Each business has support staff who handle complaint tickets, complex requests needing manual intervention, and sensitive processes such as refunds, returns, and discounts that fall outside the assistant's automatic handling ability. - The business uploads its own knowledge documents in the supported formats (Plaintext, PDF, XLSX, CSV) and updates them when policies change. - The business provides business APIs according to the exact specification for the agent to integrate with. --- ## 9. Constraints - All sample business data and the test suite are synthetic and small in scale; quality measurement results only reflect the test suite built by the group and do not represent real business data. - The Messenger channel runs in development mode, serves only test accounts, and only messages within the 24-hour window. - All customers, orders, appointments, and phone numbers in the sample data are synthetic; the sample businesses are fictional and do not match any operating business.

You are a helpful personal assistant. Maintain clear, direct, and factual communication in English.

Operational Rules:
- Only manipulate files and memory using your registered tools. If a task cannot be solved with the available tools, state the limitation directly instead of guessing.
- Only claim a file or memory was read, written, or deleted after receiving a successful tool result (ok: true).
- When a tool returns an error, report the error directly and adapt your plan; never fabricate results.

Workspace and Capabilities:
- Workspace file paths are always relative to the workspace directory (e.g. output/summary.md, skills/authoring-skills/references/skill-template.md).
- list_files lists direct directory entries. read_file reads UTF-8 text files across the workspace.
- write_file writes UTF-8 text files strictly under output/ or skills/<slug>/.
- There is no shell or terminal tool in this system. All interactions occur through file, skill, and memory tools.

Memory System:
You have access to a durable file-system memory repository structured as a two-layer contract: (bucket, name).
- Bucket "/" is strictly reserved for the user profile: name must be "profile".
  Example: memory_read("/", "profile"), memory_write("/", "profile", description="...", content="...").
  Only "profile" is permitted in bucket "/". "profile" is prohibited in any other bucket.
- Domain buckets organize specific topics and workstreams:
  - "topics": Cross-project durable domains: preferences, hardware/system environment, models, and workflows.
  - "areas": Project-specific or workstream-specific facts and status.
  Example: memory_read("topics", "ai-preferences"), memory_write("areas", "project-x", description="...", content="...").

Memory Rules & Policy:
- Trigger Policy: Only save memory upon explicit user request or explicit confirmation of a durable fact. Do not store transient queries, temporary tasks, or inferences.
- Sensitive Data: Never store credentials, secrets, API keys, or government identifiers. Do not store health, politics, or religion unless the user explicitly requests it.
- Write Procedure:
  1. Use memory_list(bucket=...) to explore existing memories.
  2. Use memory_read(bucket, name) before modifying or replacing an existing memory item.
  3. Use memory_write(bucket, name, description, content) with a single-line, keyword-dense description (1-300 chars) and a body formatted as flat bullets with no Markdown headings ('#').
  4. Confirm updates only after receiving ok: true.
- Freshness: Newly written memory takes effect on the next conversational turn.

{"ok": true, "bucket": "areas", "name": "se373-bizcare-project", "description": "BizCare helpdesk agent project spec (SE373 Group 02): scope, 6 use cases, K1-K8 knowledge areas, quality thresholds, sample workspaces, architecture", "content": "- Project: BizCare - AI customer support (CSKH) platform for small Vietnamese businesses, multi-tenant. SE373 Group 02, dated 18/10/2026.
- Architecture principle: agent = model + harness. Model generates text/decides; harness provides workspace KB access, realizes actions via tools, accesses customer profile memory, masks PII, stores traces.
- Channels: website chat widget + Facebook Messenger (dev mode, 24h window). Software: business Portal, customer channel, staff Inbox.
- Roles: business owner/workspace admin, support agent (CSKH staff), end customer.
- 6 use cases: 3.3 intent classification + entity extraction (owner Hoang, K1/K5, >=60 scenarios); 3.4 FAQ/policy answers with citations (owner Long, K3/K7, >=35 scenarios); 3.5 order/appointment lookup via tools (owner Tho, K1/K2, >=15 scenarios); 3.6 ticket creation + status update (owner Tho, K2/K5); 3.7 multi-turn memory + returning customer profile (owner Thuan, K4/K8, >=10 scenarios, one conversation >=40 messages); 3.8 reviewer agent checks answer before sending (owner Hung, K6/K7).
- Knowledge areas K1-K8: K1 model integration/structured output/agent loop; K2 tool use + agent skills; K3 RAG + KB; K4 memory/state/context; K5 workflow orchestration + human-in-the-loop; K6 multi-agent or MCP; K7 verification + evaluation; K8 security/governance/observability.
- Sample workspaces (fictional): moc-mien-florist (retail flowers, Can Tho, 29 docs) and iron-viet-fitness (gym services, HCMC, 20 docs). Each has >=20 docs in 4 format groups: Plaintext (TXT/MD/HTML), PDF, Tables (CSV/XLSX). Each has a policy file (refund threshold, return days, max discount, approval categories) and a brand voice file (form of address, tone, forbidden words, answer length).
- KB design: document store (originals, versions, effective status) + vector database (embedded chunks), sharing doc_id. Chunk metadata required: doc_id, workspace_id, title, uri, section, chunk_index, updated_at, doc_type (markdown/html/pdf/csv/xlsx), version, status (active/superseded).
- Vector DB requirement (spec 2.2.b): ONE COLLECTION PER WORKSPACE; agent locked to its workspace; no cross-collection queries; combined semantic + BM25 keyword retrieval merged before ranking; business-owner-set relevance score threshold; expired docs excluded at metadata filter step, not at ranking.
- Ingestion pipeline: validate input -> normalize -> structure-aware chunking -> embed + index -> mark superseded -> status pending/indexing/indexed/failed.
- Workflow: LangGraph, 7 nodes (receive+normalize, load state+profile, mask PII, extract intent + branch, review draft max 2 revision rounds, send to original channel, save state + write trace).
- Harness layers: workflow/checkpoint, tool, skills (5 reusable: intent extraction, policy answering, business lookup, ticket classification, answer checking), KB/RAG, memory, PII masking, reviewer, observability (run ID, trace with nodes/passages/tool calls/review/tokens/cost), test suite.
- Tools: search_knowledge (read), business lookup tools (read, phone match required), task execution tools (write, needs explicit customer confirmation), create_ticket (write, no duplicate within 24h, summary <=300 chars), update_ticket (write, agent cannot resolve/close), get_ticket/list_tickets (read), get/update_customer_profile (allowlist fields, retention limit), send_message (write, only after reviewer approves).
- Tool constraints: 5s timeout default, max 2 retries, max 6 tool calls per message turn, friendly error on API failure, never fabricate results, redirect to ticket on API error.
- Quality thresholds: schema-valid output 100%; intent accuracy >=85%; entity F1 >=0.85; Recall@5 >=0.85; valid citations 100%; faithfulness >=0.9; out-of-KB questions answered "no info" 100%; correct tool+params >=90%; no disclosure on mismatched verification 100%; ticket schema valid 100%; ticket classification >=85%, priority >=80%; 0 duplicate tickets, 100% invalid transitions blocked; compaction summary keeps 5 items 100%; PII masked 100%; returning customer uses >=1 profile item in >=80% scenarios; reviewer error detection >=80%, false block <=15%; reviewer has no write/send tools 100%. Report tokens/cost/latency (mean + p95). Test suite run at least twice (before and after improvement).
- Safety: AI transparency notice on first message + widget; workspace isolation; secrets encrypted at rest, not in source, not in widget embed/logs/trace; no money/discount commitments (reviewer blocks); >=6 prompt injection + impersonation attack scenarios in test suite.
- Out of scope: voice/video, Zalo OA/Instagram/TikTok/email, approval-gated refund/return/discount workflows, advanced urgency-based handoff, auto website crawling, MCP server exposure, on-demand aggregate reports, ERP/POS/payment gateway, e-invoicing.
- Constraints: all sample data synthetic and small scale; Messenger dev mode only; sample businesses fictional.
- English translation of the full spec written to output/project-spec-en.md.", "bytes": 5218, "updated": "2026-10-23T07:42:49.308666+00:00"}

{"ok": true, "path": "output/vector-db-decision.md", "content": "# Vector Database Decision Record — SE373 Final Project (BizCare)

**Context:** Single host, 4 vCPU / 12 GB RAM. Must co-host: Python backend, relational DB, vector DB, object storage, and a small text embedding model.
**Requirements:** strong per-workspace data isolation, BM25-equivalent full-text search *alongside* vector similarity, vector search and full-text search independently callable, hybrid search preferred but optional, client-server (not embedded), low memory footprint.
**Spec source:** `output/project-spec-en.md` (BizCare, SE373 Group 02, 18/10/2026).

---

## 1. Recommendation

**Primary: Qdrant (self-hosted, client-server).**

**Lightweight alternative: Redis Stack (RediSearch + vector sets)** if you want the absolute smallest footprint and can accept a less mature vector API.

**Fallback: pgvector** if you are willing to drop the "separate vector DB server" preference — it is by far the cheapest option, but it does not give you BM25.

---

## 2. Why Qdrant fits this host

| Requirement | How Qdrant satisfies it |
|---|---|
| Client-server | Native REST (`:6333`) + gRPC (`:6334`) server; official Python client over gRPC. |
| Vector similarity | HNSW index, cosine / dot / Euclid. |
| BM25 full-text | Payload **text index** (BM25 scoring) on any text field, independent of the vector index. |
| Independent vector vs. FTS | Two separate query paths: `VectorQuery` and `MatchText`. Neither requires the other. |
| Hybrid search | `FusionQuery` with RRF (or DBSF) over two `Prefetch` branches. |
| Per-workspace isolation | One collection per workspace (spec 2.2.b) + a `workspace_id` payload filter on every query. |
| Low memory | int8 scalar / binary / product quantization, `on_disk` vectors, `on_disk_payload`, mmap'd segments, `memmap_threshold_kb`. |
| License | Apache 2.0 — no open-core feature gating for the features above. |

### Why not the others

- **Weaviate** — best-in-class built-in multi-tenancy and BM25+vector hybrid, but it is the heaviest of the realistic options (plan for 2–4 GB RSS). On a 12 GB shared host with Postgres, MinIO, and an embedding model loaded, it leaves too little headroom. Its Go runtime + segment cache does not release memory back to the OS as aggressively.
- **Milvus (standalone)** — requires etcd **and** MinIO **and** the Milvus process. Three extra services on 4 vCPU is not viable here. (Milvus Lite is embedded and Python-only, so it fails the client-server requirement.)
- **Elasticsearch / OpenSearch** — superb BM25 and RRF hybrid, but JVM heap + off-heap Lucene structures typically cost 3–5 GB. It is a search engine being used as a vector DB; the memory cost is not justified at this scale.
- **Chroma** — client-server mode exists but is not production-grade, has no BM25, and holds the index in the client process.
- **pgvector** — cheapest by far (no extra process), but Postgres FTS uses `ts_rank`, which is *not* BM25, and hybrid ranking must be hand-rolled in SQL. It also conflicts with your stated client-server preference.
- **LanceDB / txtai** — embedded only. Disqualified.
- **Typesense** — good BM25, but the index is fully in-memory and vector support is comparatively recent.

---

## 3. Memory budget (12 GB host)

Assumed: ~1M chunks × 384 dims, single-node, Docker.

| Component | Typical RSS | Tuning lever |
|---|---|---|
| OS + Docker daemon | 0.5 – 1.0 GB | — |
| FastAPI backend + int8 embedding model | 0.5 – 0.9 GB | ONNX Runtime, int8 weights |
| PostgreSQL 16 | 1.5 – 2.5 GB | `shared_buffers = 1GB` |
| MinIO (single node) | 0.3 – 0.6 GB | small disk, no erasure coding |
| **Qdrant** (on-disk payload, int8 quant) | **0.5 – 1.5 GB** | quantization + `on_disk` |
| **Total** | **3.3 – 6.5 GB** | ~5 GB headroom |

Swap the Qdrant row to compare:

| Vector DB | Vector DB RSS | Total stack | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qdrant | 0.5 – 1.5 GB | 3.3 – 6.5 GB | Comfortable |
| Redis Stack | 0.3 – 1.0 GB | 3.1 – 6.0 GB | Comfortable, least mature vector API |
| Weaviate | 2.0 – 4.0 GB | 4.8 – 8.5 GB | Tight but workable |
| Elasticsearch / OpenSearch | 3.0 – 5.0 GB | 5.8 – 9.5 GB | Risky |
| Milvus standalone | 4.0 – 6.0 GB (+ etcd + MinIO) | 8.0 – 12.0 GB+ | Does not fit |

### 3.1 Per-workspace collections: the memory caveat

The spec (2.2.b) requires **one collection per workspace**. Qdrant allocates a minimum segment size per collection, so N collections cost more than one shared collection with N filters. With only 2 sample workspaces this is negligible. If the number of workspaces grows, options in order of preference:

1. Keep per-workspace collections but raise `memmap_threshold_kb` so small collections stay mmap'd on disk.
2. Use `shard_key_selector` with `workspace_id` as the shard key inside one collection — this gives the same logical isolation with one set of segments.
3. Fall back to a shared collection with a mandatory `workspace_id` filter (the design used in the earlier draft of `retrieval.py`).

Option 2 is the best of both worlds and is worth benchmarking before the demo.

---

## 4. Embedding model (keep it small)

| Model | Params | Dims | fp32 / int8 | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | 22.7 M | 384 | 90 MB / 23 MB | English-only corpus |
| `multilingual-e5-small` | 118 M | 384 | 470 MB / 120 MB | **Vietnamese / mixed-language corpus** |
| `paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` | 118 M | 384 | 470 MB / 120 MB | Multilingual, slightly stronger |

Recommendation for a VNUHCM project: **`multilingual-e5-small`**, int8-quantized, served via ONNX Runtime inside the backend process. E5 models need the `query:` / `passage:` prefix — bake that into your ingest and query helpers so it is never forgotten.

The corpus is Vietnamese (spec 1.4.1), so `multilingual-e5-small` is the right default. Note the spec also requires handling unaccented and abbreviated text (EV-INTENT-02); test whether the embedding model degrades on unaccented Vietnamese, and consider a text normalization step (add diacritics back) before embedding if recall suffers.

---

## 5. Isolation design (revised to match the spec)

The spec mandates **one collection per workspace** (2.2.b), so the earlier "one shared collection + tenant filter" design was replaced. The revised design has two layers of defence:

1. **Collection boundary** — `ws_<workspace_id>`. A query against the wrong collection returns nothing.
2. **Payload filter** — every query additionally pins `workspace_id` and excludes `status != active`.

Rules to enforce:

1. `workspace_id` is a `KEYWORD` payload field with an index.
2. The collection name is derived from the authenticated session, never from a request body. The agent has no ability to choose a different workspace (spec 2.2.b).
3. Every read path goes through a single wrapper that injects the filter. No raw client calls in route handlers.
4. Expired (`superseded`) documents are excluded at the **metadata filter step**, not deferred to ranking (spec 2.2.b).
5. The relevance score threshold is set by the business owner in the agent config; chunks below it must not be used to answer (spec 2.2.b, 3.4.a).
6. Regression test: insert a doc in workspace A, assert workspace B's vector, FTS, and hybrid queries all return zero hits.

---

## 6. Query patterns

See `output/retrieval.py` for the full implementation. Summary:

- **Vector only** → `query_points(query=VectorQuery(vector=v), query_filter=workspace_filter)`
- **Full-text only** → `query_points(query=MatchText(text=q, field="body"), query_filter=workspace_filter)`
- **Hybrid** → `query_points(prefetch=[VectorQuery(...), MatchText(...)], query=FusionQuery(fusion=Fusion.RRF))`

All three are independently callable; hybrid is a composition of the other two, not a separate subsystem. The spec (2.2.b) requires the combined form for production retrieval; the other two remain available for the evaluation harness and for debugging.

---

## 7. Deployment checklist

1. `docker compose up -d` with the provided `output/docker-compose.yml` (mem limits are set per service to enforce the budget).
2. Create the collection with the text index and int8 quantization (see `retrieval.py::ensure_collection`).
3. Ingest with `workspace_id` stamped server-side and the full spec metadata set.
4. Smoke-test: vector-only, FTS-only, hybrid, the cross-workspace isolation test, and the superseded-exclusion test.
5. Monitor `docker stats` — if Qdrant exceeds ~2 GB, enable `on_disk_payload` and re-index with product quantization.

---

## 8. Decision log

- **Chose Qdrant over Weaviate** — memory headroom on a 12 GB shared host outweighs Weaviate's superior first-class multi-tenancy, since Qdrant covers isolation via per-workspace collections.
- **Chose Qdrant over Elasticsearch** — BM25 quality is not the bottleneck at this data scale; RAM is.
- **Kept a separate vector server** (per stated preference) rather than pgvector, but documented pgvector as the fallback if the host turns out to be smaller than specified.
- **Revised isolation design from shared-collection to per-workspace collections** after reading the spec (2.2.b), which explicitly requires a collection per workspace and forbids cross-collection queries.
- **Kept `multilingual-e5-small`** rather than an English-only model, because the corpus and all test scenarios are Vietnamese.
"}

{"ok": true, "path": "output/retrieval.py", "content": """"
SE373 final project - BizCare retrieval layer (Qdrant).

Implements the knowledge base requirements from the project spec (section 2.2):

  - One collection per workspace (spec 2.2.b). The agent is locked to the
    workspace it is operating in; no query ever spans all collections.
  - Combined semantic + keyword (BM25) retrieval, with the two result
    lists merged before ranking (spec 2.2.b).
  - A relevance score threshold set by the business owner; chunks below
    the threshold must not be used to answer (spec 2.2.b, 3.4.a).
  - Expired documents are removed at the metadata filter step, not
    deferred to the ranking step (spec 2.2.b).
  - Chunk metadata matches the spec table exactly (spec 2.2.b).

The three query paths are independently callable:
  1. vector_search()   - dense similarity only
  2. fulltext_search() - BM25 only
  3. hybrid_search()   - RRF fusion of the two (spec 2.2.b requires the
                         combined form; the other two remain available
                         for debugging and for the evaluation harness)

Install:  pip install qdrant-client
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Sequence

from qdrant_client import QdrantClient, models

QDRANT_URL = "http://localhost:6333"

# Embedding model must match the one used at ingest time.
# For a Vietnamese / mixed-language corpus use multilingual-e5-small (384 dims).
# For English-only use all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384 dims).
EMBED_DIM = 384
EMBED_MODEL = "multilingual-e5-small"

# E5 models require asymmetric prefixes. Bake them in here so they are
# never forgotten at call sites.
QUERY_PREFIX = "query: "
PASSAGE_PREFIX = "passage: "

# Chunk status values (spec 2.2.b metadata table).
STATUS_ACTIVE = "active"
STATUS_SUPERSEDED = "superseded"

# Document types (spec 2.2.b metadata table).
DOC_TYPES = ("markdown", "html", "pdf", "csv", "xlsx")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Client
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_client() -> QdrantClient:
    # Prefer gRPC for lower latency and less per-request overhead.
    return QdrantClient(url=QDRANT_URL, prefer_grpc=True, timeout=30)


def collection_name(workspace_id: str) -> str:
    """One collection per workspace (spec 2.2.b).

    The workspace id comes from the authenticated session, never from a
    request body. The agent has no ability to choose a different one.
    """
    return f"ws_{workspace_id}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collection setup
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ensure_collection(client: QdrantClient, workspace_id: str) -> None:
    """Create the workspace collection with a BM25 text index and int8 quantization."""
    name = collection_name(workspace_id)
    if client.collection_exists(name):
        return

    client.create_collection(
        collection_name=name,
        vectors_config=models.VectorParams(
            size=EMBED_DIM,
            distance=models.Distance.COSINE,
            on_disk=False,  # vectors stay in RAM; payload goes to disk
        ),
        # BM25 full-text index over the chunk body.
        # This index is completely independent of the HNSW vector index.
        hnsw_config=models.HnswConfigDiff(
            m=16,
            ef_construct=100,
            on_disk=False,
        ),
        quantization_config=models.ScalarQuantization(
            scalar=models.ScalarQuantizationConfig(
                type=models.ScalarType.INT8,
                quantile=0.99,
                always_ram=False,
            )
        ),
        optimizers_config=models.OptimizersConfigDiff(
            memmap_threshold=20_000,
            indexing_threshold=20_000,
        ),
    )

    # Payload schema. workspace_id is a KEYWORD index -> fast, exact filtering.
    client.create_payload_index(
        collection_name=name,
        field_name="workspace_id",
        field_schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    )
    client.create_payload_index(
        collection_name=name,
        field_name="doc_id",
        field_schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    )
    client.create_payload_index(
        collection_name=name,
        field_name="status",
        field_schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    )
    client.create_payload_index(
        collection_name=name,
        field_name="version",
        field_schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    )
    client.create_payload_index(
        collection_name=name,
        field_name="updated_at",
        field_schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.DATETIME,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filtering
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def workspace_filter(workspace_id: str) -> models.Filter:
    """The only sanctioned way to build a workspace filter.

    Two layers of defence:
      1. The collection itself is per-workspace, so a wrong collection
         name is already a hard boundary.
      2. The payload filter additionally pins workspace_id and excludes
         expired documents at the metadata filter step (spec 2.2.b).
    """
    return models.Filter(
        must=[
            models.FieldCondition(
                key="workspace_id",
                match=models.MatchValue(value=workspace_id),
            ),
            models.FieldCondition(
                key="status",
                match=models.MatchValue(value=STATUS_ACTIVE),
            ),
        ]
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingest
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Chunk:
    """A chunk of a document, with the metadata fields required by the spec."""

    doc_id: str
    text: str
    title: str
    uri: str
    section: str
    chunk_index: int
    updated_at: datetime
    doc_type: str
    version: str
    status: str = STATUS_ACTIVE
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.doc_type not in DOC_TYPES:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid doc_type: {self.doc_type}")
        if self.status not in (STATUS_ACTIVE, STATUS_SUPERSEDED):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid status: {self.status}")


def upsert_chunks(
    client: QdrantClient,
    workspace_id: str,
    chunks: Sequence[Chunk],
    embeddings: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
) -> None:
    """Write chunks for one workspace.

    workspace_id is stamped here from the authenticated session, never
    taken from the request body.
    """
    if len(chunks) != len(embeddings):
        raise ValueError("chunks and embeddings length mismatch")

    points = [
        models.PointStruct(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            vector=list(vec),
            payload={
                "workspace_id": workspace_id,   # server-side stamp
                "doc_id": chunk.doc_id,
                "title": chunk.title,
                "uri": chunk.uri,
                "section": chunk.section,
                "chunk_index": chunk.chunk_index,
                "updated_at": chunk.updated_at,
                "doc_type": chunk.doc_type,
                "version": chunk.version,
                "status": chunk.status,
                "body": chunk.text,   # the BM25-indexed field
                **chunk.extra,
            },
        )
        for chunk, vec in zip(chunks, embeddings)
    ]

    client.upsert(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        points=points,
        wait=True,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Query path 1: vector similarity only
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def vector_search(
    client: QdrantClient,
    workspace_id: str,
    query_vector: Sequence[float],
    limit: int = 10,
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
) -> list[models.ScoredPoint]:
    """Dense retrieval. Does not touch the full-text index at all.

    score_threshold is the business owner's relevance threshold
    (spec 2.2.b). Chunks below it must not be used to answer.
    """
    return client.query_points(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        query=models.VectorQuery(
            vector=list(query_vector),
            limit=limit,
            score_threshold=score_threshold,
        ),
        query_filter=workspace_filter(workspace_id),
        with_payload=True,
    ).points


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Query path 2: BM25 full-text only
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def fulltext_search(
    client: QdrantClient,
    workspace_id: str,
    query_text: str,
    limit: int = 10,
) -> list[models.ScoredPoint]:
    """BM25 retrieval over the 'body' payload field.

    Does not touch the vector index at all. The returned score is the
    BM25 score, not a cosine similarity.
    """
    return client.query_points(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        query=models.MatchText(
            text=query_text,
            field="body",
        ),
        query_filter=workspace_filter(workspace_id),
        limit=limit,
        with_payload=True,
    ).points


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Query path 3: hybrid (semantic + keyword merged before ranking)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def hybrid_search(
    client: QdrantClient,
    workspace_id: str,
    query_vector: Sequence[float],
    query_text: str,
    limit: int = 10,
    fusion: models.Fusion = models.Fusion.RRF,
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
) -> list[models.ScoredPoint]:
    """Reciprocal Rank Fusion over the vector and BM25 branches.

    Each branch is a Prefetch, so both are executed independently and
    their ranked lists are merged before the final ranking (spec 2.2.b).
    RRF is rank-based and needs no score normalization, which is why it
    is preferred over DBSF here.
    """
    return client.query_points(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        prefetch=[
            models.Prefetch(
                query=models.VectorQuery(vector=list(query_vector), limit=limit * 2),
                filter=workspace_filter(workspace_id),
            ),
            models.Prefetch(
                query=models.MatchText(text=query_text, field="body"),
                filter=workspace_filter(workspace_id),
            ),
        ],
        query=models.FusionQuery(fusion=fusion),
        limit=limit,
        score_threshold=score_threshold,
        with_payload=True,
    ).points


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Versioning (spec 2.2.c)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def supersede_document(
    client: QdrantClient,
    workspace_id: str,
    doc_id: str,
    new_version: str,
) -> None:
    """Mark every chunk of the current version as superseded.

    The old chunks stay in the vector database but are filtered out at
    the metadata filter step, so they never reach the candidate set.
    The document store keeps the old version for history and trace
    reconciliation.
    """
    client.set_payload(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        payload={"status": STATUS_SUPERSEDED},
        points_selector=models.FilterSelector(
            filter=models.Filter(
                must=[
                    models.FieldCondition(key="workspace_id",
                                         match=models.MatchValue(value=workspace_id)),
                    models.FieldCondition(key="doc_id",
                                         match=models.MatchValue(value=doc_id)),
                    models.FieldCondition(key="status",
                                         match=models.MatchValue(value=STATUS_ACTIVE)),
                ]
            )
        ),
        wait=True,
    )


def delete_document(client: QdrantClient, workspace_id: str, doc_id: str) -> None:
    """Soft delete: remove from the vector database, keep the document
    store record for reconciling old traces (spec 2.2.c)."""
    client.delete(
        collection_name=collection_name(workspace_id),
        points_selector=models.FilterSelector(
            filter=models.Filter(
                must=[
                    models.FieldCondition(key="workspace_id",
                                         match=models.MatchValue(value=workspace_id)),
                    models.FieldCondition(key="doc_id",
                                         match=models.MatchValue(value=doc_id)),
                ]
            )
        ),
        wait=True,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Isolation regression test
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_isolation(client: QdrantClient, embed_fn) -> None:
    """Insert a doc in workspace A, assert workspace B sees nothing.

    Run this in CI. It is the single most important test for the
    workspace isolation requirement (spec 3.4.b criterion 6, 3.7.b
    criterion 6).
    """
    ws_a, ws_b = "moc-mien-florist", "iron-viet-fitness"
    marker = "zzz-isolation-marker-9f3a"
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    for ws in (ws_a, ws_b):
        ensure_collection(client, ws)

    upsert_chunks(
        client,
        ws_a,
        [
            Chunk(
                doc_id="iso-1",
                text=f"{marker} confidential content",
                title="Isolation test",
                uri="test://iso-1",
                section="Test",
                chunk_index=0,
                updated_at=now,
                doc_type="markdown",
                version="v1",
            )
        ],
        [embed_fn(PASSAGE_PREFIX + marker + " confidential content")],
    )

    vec = embed_fn(QUERY_PREFIX + marker)

    a_vec = vector_search(client, ws_a, vec, limit=5)
    b_vec = vector_search(client, ws_b, vec, limit=5)
    a_txt = fulltext_search(client, ws_a, marker, limit=5)
    b_txt = fulltext_search(client, ws_b, marker, limit=5)
    a_hyb = hybrid_search(client, ws_a, vec, marker, limit=5)
    b_hyb = hybrid_search(client, ws_b, vec, marker, limit=5)

    assert a_vec, "workspace A should find its own document"
    assert a_txt, "workspace A should find its own document via BM25"
    assert a_hyb, "workspace A should find its own document via hybrid"

    assert not b_vec, "ISOLATION FAIL: workspace B saw workspace A vector results"
    assert not b_txt, "ISOLATION FAIL: workspace B saw workspace A full-text results"
    assert not b_hyb, "ISOLATION FAIL: workspace B saw workspace A hybrid results"

    print("isolation OK: vector, full-text and hybrid all workspace-scoped")


def test_superseded_excluded(client: QdrantClient, embed_fn) -> None:
    """A superseded document must not appear in any result set.

    Covers spec 3.4.c EV-POLICY-07.
    """
    ws = "moc-mien-florist"
    marker = "zzz-superseded-marker-4b1e"
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    upsert_chunks(
        client,
        ws,
        [
            Chunk(
                doc_id="sup-1",
                text=f"{marker} old policy text",
                title="Old policy",
                uri="test://sup-1",
                section="Policy",
                chunk_index=0,
                updated_at=now,
                doc_type="markdown",
                version="v1",
            )
        ],
        [embed_fn(PASSAGE_PREFIX + marker + " old policy text")],
    )

    assert fulltext_search(client, ws, marker, limit=5), "precondition: doc is active"

    supersede_document(client, ws, "sup-1", new_version="v2")

    assert not fulltext_search(client, ws, marker, limit=5), \
        "SUPERSEDED FAIL: expired document still returned by BM25"
    assert not vector_search(client, ws, embed_fn(QUERY_PREFIX + marker), limit=5), \
        "SUPERSEDED FAIL: expired document still returned by vector search"

    print("superseded exclusion OK")
"}

Section numbering is preserved so it can be cited directly in the technical report. --- ## 1. Overview BizCare is an AI-powered customer support (CSKH) platform for small businesses in Vietnam, operating on a multi-tenant model. Each business has its own workspace where it uploads its own knowledge documents and configures its assistant. A business can integrate the assistant into its own website (via a chat widget) or its Facebook fanpage (Messenger chatbot). The assistant understands intent and extracts information from customer messages to answer questions about products, services, and policies with source citations. It looks up orders and appointments, or creates a ticket for complaints it cannot resolve. BizCare supports remembering conversation context and customer profiles for returning customers. The product is built on the **agent = model + harness** architecture. The model generates text and makes decisions. The harness gives the model access to the workspace knowledge base, realizes action decisions through tools that connect to the business's systems, and accesses the customer profile memory. Beyond interacting with the model, the harness masks personal data to protect customer privacy, and stores traces for auditing. ### 1.1. Background Most questions small businesses receive through CSKH channels such as a Messenger fanpage or a chat window on the business website tend to repeat: product/service pricing, stock availability, shipping status, return/warranty policies, or basic usage instructions. Support staff get overloaded during peak hours. A CSKH chatbot that answers policies incorrectly, promises arbitrary discounts, or leaks customer data causes real harm to the business. BizCare addresses both problems: the assistant handles repetitive questions to reduce the load on support staff, while being constrained so it does not answer policies incorrectly, does not make arbitrary promises, and does not leak customer data. The main features of BizCare: - **Grounded answers:** the assistant answers questions about pricing, services, and policies based on documents the business itself uploaded, with source citations so customers and staff can verify. If a question falls outside the documents, the assistant says clearly that it has no information rather than guessing. - **Understands messages as real customers write them:** the assistant reads abbreviated, unaccented, emoji-containing, or multi-intent messages; extracts the intent and the required information (order code, phone number, product, date/time...) on its own, and only asks back for what is still missing. - **Accurate order and appointment lookup:** the assistant automatically looks up order status, stock availability, and supports direct appointment operations through the business's systems. - **No dropped requests:** complaints and requests that are not resolved become tickets; the customer receives a ticket code and can ask for progress later. - **Remembers customers:** the assistant maintains long conversation threads, recognizes returning customers, and reuses information the customer previously provided, such as preferred form of address or frequently purchased shoe size. - **Checks before sending:** every answer is reviewed by a separate agent for policy, brand voice, and data safety; answers that fail are corrected or blocked, for example when they contain refund, return, or discount commitments. - **Data protection:** sensitive customer information (national ID card number, card number, OTP, password) is masked before being stored; each business's data lives in its own workspace, isolated from other businesses. ### 1.2. Objectives 1. Answers are grounded in documents and carry citations as evidence. 2. Questions outside the knowledge base are answered with a "no information available" template and a request to create a support ticket. 3. Order status, stock availability, and appointment operations are performed accurately through tools integrated with a customer identity verification mechanism. 4. Complaints and unresolved requests are recorded as structured tickets with a trackable lifecycle. 5. Long-term context is maintained, returning customers are recognized, and customer personal data is protected. 6. The number of incorrect answers reaching customers is reduced through the reviewer. 7. All behavior is measurable and verifiable with a test suite. ### 1.3. Users | Role | Main activities on the system | |---|---| | Business owner / workspace admin | Register a workspace; upload knowledge documents; configure the assistant (name, greeting, brand voice, working hours); configure the business; obtain the widget embed code or connect a fanpage. | | Support agent (CSKH staff) | View and handle tickets created by the agent; receive requests that need manual handling; update ticket status; look up the trace of each agent turn. | | End customer | Chat with the assistant via the website widget or the fanpage's Messenger to ask questions, look up orders and appointments, or submit a support request. | ### 1.4. Scope #### 1.4.1. In scope - Understanding Vietnamese text. Including abbreviations, unaccented text, emoji, multiple intents in one message. - Website chat widget and/or Facebook Messenger channels. - Agent features covering all six use cases defined in section 3. - Software consisting of the business Portal, the customer channel, and the staff Inbox. - Integration with the business's systems via API. #### 1.4.2. Out of scope - Voice calls, video calls, speech recognition. - Zalo OA, Instagram, TikTok, email. - Refund, return, and discount workflows that require human approval. - Advanced automatic conversation classification and handoff based on urgency. - Automatic website crawling to build the knowledge base. - Exposing the tool set as an MCP server. - Generating aggregate reports on demand for the business owner. - ERP, POS, and payment gateway integrations. - Electronic invoice issuance. #### 1.4.3. Handling out-of-scope requests Customer messages may still contain out-of-scope intents (refund, return, discount, or a request for staff intervention). For these intents, the assistant makes no commitment whatsoever about money or promotions. The assistant answers with general information available in the knowledge base (for example, return conditions) if it exists, then creates a ticket with the extracted information for support staff to handle. --- ## 2.
